insights.headline: MCX gold reclaims Rs 1.50 lakh as soft US inflation cuts October Fed-hike odds to 38%
insights.summary: Gold steadied on Thursday after softer US inflation data pushed October Fed-hike odds down to 38%, with MCX gold crossing Rs 1.50 lakh intraday and silver surging over Rs 3,000 per kg. Experts see prices firm but range-bound into the festive season as Dussehra, Dhanteras, Diwali and winter wedding demand meet record prices. Friday's US nonfarm payrolls is the next macro trigger; SGB investors face the first October premature-redemption deadline on Oct 5.
points: Softer August US PCE cut October Fed-hike odds to 38% from 45%; Goldman Sachs pushed its next-hike call to December.
MCX gold crossed Rs 1.50 lakh intraday (Dec futures Rs 1,50,470); silver jumped over Rs 3,000 to Rs 2,26,350 per kg.
Experts expect firm, range-bound prices through the festive season; record prices may shift buyers to lighter jewellery, coins and digital gold.
IDFC First Bank expects further rupee depreciation in H2FY27 as RBI intervention turns more cautious; reserves stand at $765.9 billion.
Friday's US nonfarm payrolls is next; four SGB tranches face RBI premature redemption in October, first deadline Oct 5.

trending.title: Fed policy pivot expectations
trending.summary: Soft PCE data cut October-hike odds to 38% and pushed Goldman's hike call to December; Friday's payrolls is the next decider for bullion.

trending.title: Festive demand meets record prices
trending.summary: Diwali-season demand is the big question: experts see range-bound prices with buyers shifting to lighter jewellery, coins and digital gold as MCX gold reclaims Rs 1.50 lakh.

trending.title: Rupee and yields squeeze on Indian buyers
trending.summary: Further rupee depreciation is expected in H2FY27 while multi-decade-high US yields keep weighing on non-yielding bullion.

trending.title: Silver outperforming gold again
trending.summary: Silver surged over Rs 3,000 intraday on MCX, continuing to outpace gold after its steeper 13.5% September fall.

trending.title: SGB exit window narrows
trending.summary: Four SGB tranches face RBI premature redemption in October — the first deadline is days away and the tax exemption is maturity-only from FY27.

items.title: Gold inches higher as softer US inflation dims October Fed hike bets
items.summary: Gold edged up Thursday after soft US inflation data cooled October Fed-hike bets, Reuters reports. Spot gold rose 0.5% to $4,175.19 after August PCE came in below forecasts; December futures gained 0.4% to $4,204.80. October-hike odds fell to 38% from 45%, though a December move is still priced at 97%. A firm dollar capped gains; silver rose 1.2% to $61.11. Friday’s payrolls report is next.

items.title: Goldman Sachs pushes Fed rate hike forecast to December
items.summary: Goldman Sachs pushed its next-hike call to December after August PCE inflation printed 3.4% versus 3.7% expected, Reuters reports. The brokerage had forecast a 25bp October hike. "We see a strong chance the FOMC will ultimately conclude additional rate hikes are unnecessary," it said. October-hike odds fell to 38% from 71% a week ago, per CME FedWatch. Friday's US nonfarm payrolls report is next.

items.title: Gold price future roadmap: 6% September fall meets Diwali demand hopes
items.summary: Gold fell about 6.5% in September, its worst month since June, after Fed tightening and a 10-year US yield at 5.293% — highest since 2007, Mint reports. Brickwork Ratings' Rajeev Sharan expects firm but range-bound prices through Dussehra, Dhanteras, Diwali and winter wedding demand; Monarch PMS' Dhruv Joglekar points to festive physical buying plus central-bank accumulation.

items.title: Surging Yields Bring the Bond Market Back to the Turn of the Century
items.summary: The 10-year US Treasury yield pushed above 5.3% on Wednesday — past its 2007 peak to the highest since 2002, the Journal reports, ending at 5.292%. The milestone points to structurally elevated borrowing costs driven by government debt, the AI investment boom and trade barriers. Investors expect several more Fed hikes over the next year.

items.title: Gold Down 8.5% in Sept, Silver -13.5% as Real Yields 'Re-Price Fast'
items.summary: Gold fell 8.5% and silver 13.5% in September as real yields repriced sharply higher, BullionVault reports. Inflation-protected 10-year Treasury yields jumped the most in four years to near a record high — the most negative nine-month gold-real-yield stretch since 2020. Conventional 10-year yields still offered 5.24% at month-end after their steepest monthly rise since September 2023.

items.title: Gold Glitters, Silver Shines: Yellow Metal Prices Jump By Over Rs 1,500, White Metal Surges By More Than Rs 3,000
items.summary: MCX gold crossed Rs 1.50 lakh on Thursday, with December futures touching Rs 1,50,470 per 10g around 11:33 am — an intraday jump of over Rs 1,500, NDTV Profit reports. Silver surged more than Rs 3,000 intraday to Rs 2,26,350 per kg, up 1.18%, continuing to outperform gold. Technical indicators suggest the recovery is yet to gain decisive momentum.

items.title: Gold at Rs 1.47 lakh: Will prices rise further or stay around here?
items.summary: MCX gold held around Rs 1.47 lakh on Thursday, up 1.18% to Rs 1,47,840 near midday, India Today reports. Elevated US Treasury yields and a 14-week-high dollar index are capping bullion, though softer US inflation data briefly cut October Fed-hike bets. Analysts see consolidation rather than a one-sided move, with Friday's US nonfarm payrolls the next trigger.

items.title: Rupee to fall more, yield curve to shift higher in H2FY27: Gaura Sengupta
items.summary: IDFC First Bank chief economist Gaura Sengupta expects the rupee to depreciate further in H2FY27 as RBI intervention turns more cautious now that the FCNR(B) window has closed — the $133 billion mobilised is borrowed money to be repaid in three years. Persistent dollar strength and high US yields keep foreign capital away, pushing the G-sec yield curve higher.

items.title: Rupee remains relatively stable in H1 FY27 after 10% fall in FY26
items.summary: The rupee depreciated just 1.1% in H1FY27 after a 9.9% slide in FY26, Business Standard reports, settling at 95.83 per dollar as RBI intervention around the 96 level and special dollar-rupee swaps contained volatility. Forex reserves rose about $78 billion to $765.9 billion; the 10-year G-sec held near 7.17%. Markets now eye the RBI’s October policy meeting.

items.title: Gold, silver prices today: What investors should watch after September correction
items.summary: Gold was steady on October 1 while silver gained as investors weighed US rates, yields and the dollar, CNBC TV18 reports. COMEX gold traded at $4,191.90 (+0.12%) and silver at $60.965 (+0.66%); domestic 99.9% gold rose ₹700 to ₹1.49 lakh/10g with silver flat at ₹2.32 lakh/kg. Elevated yields cap bullion while ETF holdings rose five days straight; the Oct 2 US jobs report is next.

items.title: BOK to add gold to its coffers for the first time since 2013
items.summary: The Bank of Korea will buy about one metric ton of domestically produced gold in December — its first physical purchase since February 2013, Aju Press reports. A settlement system completes December 14; the gold will be bought in won via KRX/KSD from domestic output. The BOK held 104.4 tonnes at end-August and resumed gold exposure via a $250 million gold ETF position in Q2.

items.title: SGB premature redemption October 2026: 4 tranches eligible for early exit
items.summary: RBI scheduled premature redemption for four SGB tranches — 2019-20 Series V and VI and 2020-21 Series I and VII, Livemint reports. Deadlines: Oct 5 (Series V, redeems Oct 15), Oct 9 (Series VII, Oct 19), Oct 19 (Series I, Oct 28), Oct 21 (Series VI, Oct 30). Value uses IBJA's 3-day 999-gold average. From FY27 the capital-gains exemption applies only if held to maturity, so early exit may be taxed.
